title: LA HB459: Provides relative to the use of artificial intelligence in political campaigns

obligations: No person shall make or cause to be made any electioneering communication that portrays a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that is, through the use of artificial intelligence, created, altered, or digitally manipulated in a manner that would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that would falsely appear to replace an individual's likeness with the likeness of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall without providing a clear and understandable disclosure on the electioneering communication that it was created using artificial intelligence. The form of the disclosure shall be consistent with the disclosure requirements of Subsection (E) of this Section. (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))

Any person, other than a candidate or a committee, who makes any expenditure for an electioneering communication shall file reports if such expenditures exceed one thousand dollars in the aggregate during the aggregating period as defined for committees. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1))

Coordinated expenditures made for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination or election of the candidate shall be considered a contribution to the candidate, the principal campaign committee, or the subsidiary committee thereof that cooperated, consulted, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator of or requested or suggested the creation or dissemination of the electioneering communication. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii))

Any funds of a membership organization or corporation used for expenditures for electioneering communications shall be reportable and all contributions made by such membership organization or corporation which are otherwise reportable under the provisions of this Chapter shall be reported. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))
All other expenditures made by a membership organization or business entity which are otherwise reportable under the provisions of this Chapter shall be reported. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii))
prohibitions: No person shall make or cause to be made any electioneering communication that portrays a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that is, through the use of artificial intelligence, created, altered, or digitally manipulated in a manner that would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that would falsely appear to replace an individual's likeness with the likeness of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall without providing a clear and understandable disclosure on the electioneering communication that it was created using artificial intelligence. (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))
reading.what_it_does: This law requires a clear disclosure on electioneering communications that use artificial intelligence to create, alter, or digitally manipulate the image, likeness, or voice of a candidate or elected official subject to recall so that it falsely appears authentic. It also expands campaign finance definitions and reporting requirements for persons other than candidates and committees who make expenditures for electioneering communications. It provides criminal penalties for violations with intent to injure a candidate's reputation or deceive a voter.
key_definitions: Artificial intelligence: same meaning as provided in R.S. 14:73.14 (R.S. 18:1463(F)(2)(a))
Candidate: same meaning as provided in R.S. 18:1483 (R.S. 18:1463(F)(2)(b))

Digital material: any material or communication that, for a fee or other payment, is placed or promoted on a public facing website, web application, or digital application, including a social network, advertising network, or search engine (R.S. 18:1463(G)(1))

Electioneering communication: any communication, whether printed, digital, or broadcast by a media entity, that contains express advocacy supporting or opposing the nomination or election of a person to public office, the recall of a public official, or a proposition or question submitted to the voters, or the only reasonable conclusion to be drawn from the presentation, content, and context is that it is intended to appeal for a vote in a specific election for or against a specific candidate or for or against the recall of a specific elected official or a proposition or for or against a question submitted to the voters (R.S. 18:1483(33)(a))

Media entity: includes a radio broadcast station, television broadcast station, cable or satellite television company, or other video service provider, streaming video provider, newspaper company, periodical company, billboard company, advertisement agency, or media platform responsible for the production or publication of any advertisement, voice, data, or other communications, information services, or internet access provider, or bona fide news or public interest website operator (R.S. 18:1483(33)(b))

Coordinated expenditure: an expenditure made by any person in cooperation, consultation, or concert with, or at the request or suggestion of, a candidate, his principal campaign committee or a subsidiary committee thereof, or their agents for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination or election of the candidate or of expenditures for electioneering communications (R.S. 18:1483(8))

Expenditure for a person other than a candidate or committee: a purchase, payment, advance, deposit, or gift, of money or anything of value made for an electioneering communication (R.S. 18:1483(11)(a))

Contribution includes coordinated expenditures made for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination or election of the candidate and considered a contribution to the candidate, the principal campaign committee, or the subsidiary committee thereof that, directly or through an agent, cooperated with, consulted with, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator of or requested or suggested the creation or dissemination of the electioneering communication (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii))

Contribution shall not include any dues or membership fees of any membership organization or corporation made by its members or stockholders, if such membership organization or corporation is not organized primarily for the purpose of supporting, opposing or otherwise influencing the nomination for election, or election, of any person to public office making expenditures for electioneering communications. However, any funds of such an organization or corporation used for the purpose of contributions to candidates or committees or to publicly advocate support or defeat of a candidate or for expenditures for electioneering communications shall be reportable and all contributions made by such membership organization or corporation which are otherwise reportable under the provisions of this Chapter shall be reported (R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))
compliance_steps: Determine whether a communication qualifies as an electioneering communication under R.S. 18:1483(33)(a).

If artificial intelligence is used to create, alter, or digitally manipulate the image, likeness, or voice of a candidate or elected official subject to recall in an electioneering communication, include a clear and understandable disclosure that it was created using artificial intelligence, consistent with R.S. 18:1463(E). (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))

Ensure the communication does not falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of actual speech or conduct or falsely appear to replace an individual's likeness with the likeness of a candidate or elected official subject to recall without the disclosure. (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))
Track all expenditures for electioneering communications, including digital material placed or promoted for a fee. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1), R.S. 18:1463(G)(1))
If expenditures for electioneering communications exceed one thousand dollars in the aggregate during the aggregating period, file reports as required. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1))

Treat coordinated expenditures for electioneering communications as contributions to the candidate or committee that cooperated, consulted, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii), R.S. 18:1483(8))
If operating as a media entity, ensure no input in or control over paid political announcements, advertisements, or electioneering communications to qualify for the exemption. (R.S. 18:1463(I))

If a membership organization or business entity, report all other expenditures for electioneering communications that are otherwise reportable, even if internal communications to employees, members, directors, or stockholders are excluded. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii), R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))

Candidates and elected officials subject to recall
Persons other than candidates or committees who make expenditures for electioneering communications
Media entities that broadcast paid political announcements, advertisements, or electioneering communications
Membership organizations and business entities making electioneering communications

(R.S. 18:1463(I))

Expenditure shall not include any communication, including an electioneering communication, by any membership organization or business entity to its employees, members, directors, or stockholders, or their family members, if such membership organization or business entity is not organized primarily for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination for election, or election, of any person to public office or for the purpose of supporting or opposing a proposition or question to be submitted to the voters making electioneering communications. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii))

Contribution shall not include any dues or membership fees of any membership organization or corporation made by its members or stockholders, if such membership organization or corporation is not organized primarily for the purpose of supporting, opposing or otherwise influencing the nomination for election, or election, of any person to public office making expenditures for electioneering communications. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))

(R.S. 18:1463(H)) The text does not state which agency enforces this provision or whether there is a private right of action.

(R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))

An organization that makes expenditures for electioneering communications, including digital material placed or promoted on public facing websites or applications, must file reports if those expenditures exceed one thousand dollars in the aggregate during the aggregating period. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1), R.S. 18:1463(G)(1))

Coordinated expenditures for electioneering communications are treated as contributions to the candidate or committee that cooperated, consulted, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator, which may trigger contribution limits and reporting. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii), R.S. 18:1483(8))

A media entity that broadcasts a paid political announcement, advertisement, or electioneering communication in which the broadcaster has had no input in or control over the announcement, advertisement, or electioneering communication is exempt from the provisions of this Section. (R.S. 18:1463(I))

Communications by a membership organization or business entity to its employees, members, directors, or stockholders, or their family members, are excluded from the definition of expenditure if the organization is not organized primarily for political purposes, but other expenditures for electioneering communications remain reportable. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii))

Passed 2026-06-09. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This law requires a clear disclosure on electioneering communications that use artificial intelligence to create, alter, or digitally manipulate the image, likeness, or voice of a candidate or elected official subject to recall so that it falsely appears authentic. It also expands campaign finance definitions and reporting requirements for persons other than candidates and committees who make expenditures for electioneering communications. It provides criminal penalties for violations with intent to injure a candidate's reputation or deceive a voter.

Who it applies to

  • Any person who makes or causes to be made an electioneering communication
  • Candidates and elected officials subject to recall
  • Persons other than candidates or committees who make expenditures for electioneering communications
  • Media entities that broadcast paid political announcements, advertisements, or electioneering communications
  • Membership organizations and business entities making electioneering communications

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: same meaning as provided in R.S. 14:73.14 (R.S. 18:1463(F)(2)(a))
  • Candidate: same meaning as provided in R.S. 18:1483 (R.S. 18:1463(F)(2)(b))
  • Digital material: any material or communication that, for a fee or other payment, is placed or promoted on a public facing website, web application, or digital application, including a social network, advertising network, or search engine (R.S. 18:1463(G)(1))
  • Electioneering communication: any communication, whether printed, digital, or broadcast by a media entity, that contains express advocacy supporting or opposing the nomination or election of a person to public office, the recall of a public official, or a proposition or question submitted to the voters, or the only reasonable conclusion to be drawn from the presentation, content, and context is that it is intended to appeal for a vote in a specific election for or against a specific candidate or for or against the recall of a specific elected official or a proposition or for or against a question submitted to the voters (R.S. 18:1483(33)(a))
  • Media entity: includes a radio broadcast station, television broadcast station, cable or satellite television company, or other video service provider, streaming video provider, newspaper company, periodical company, billboard company, advertisement agency, or media platform responsible for the production or publication of any advertisement, voice, data, or other communications, information services, or internet access provider, or bona fide news or public interest website operator (R.S. 18:1483(33)(b))
  • Coordinated expenditure: an expenditure made by any person in cooperation, consultation, or concert with, or at the request or suggestion of, a candidate, his principal campaign committee or a subsidiary committee thereof, or their agents for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination or election of the candidate or of expenditures for electioneering communications (R.S. 18:1483(8))
  • Expenditure for a person other than a candidate or committee: a purchase, payment, advance, deposit, or gift, of money or anything of value made for an electioneering communication (R.S. 18:1483(11)(a))
  • Contribution includes coordinated expenditures made for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination or election of the candidate and considered a contribution to the candidate, the principal campaign committee, or the subsidiary committee thereof that, directly or through an agent, cooperated with, consulted with, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator of or requested or suggested the creation or dissemination of the electioneering communication (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii))
  • Contribution shall not include any dues or membership fees of any membership organization or corporation made by its members or stockholders, if such membership organization or corporation is not organized primarily for the purpose of supporting, opposing or otherwise influencing the nomination for election, or election, of any person to public office making expenditures for electioneering communications. However, any funds of such an organization or corporation used for the purpose of contributions to candidates or committees or to publicly advocate support or defeat of a candidate or for expenditures for electioneering communications shall be reportable and all contributions made by such membership organization or corporation which are otherwise reportable under the provisions of this Chapter shall be reported (R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))

Obligations

  • No person shall make or cause to be made any electioneering communication that portrays a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that is, through the use of artificial intelligence, created, altered, or digitally manipulated in a manner that would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that would falsely appear to replace an individual's likeness with the likeness of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall without providing a clear and understandable disclosure on the electioneering communication that it was created using artificial intelligence. The form of the disclosure shall be consistent with the disclosure requirements of Subsection (E) of this Section. (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))
  • Any person, other than a candidate or a committee, who makes any expenditure for an electioneering communication shall file reports if such expenditures exceed one thousand dollars in the aggregate during the aggregating period as defined for committees. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1))
  • Coordinated expenditures made for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination or election of the candidate shall be considered a contribution to the candidate, the principal campaign committee, or the subsidiary committee thereof that cooperated, consulted, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator of or requested or suggested the creation or dissemination of the electioneering communication. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii))
  • Any funds of a membership organization or corporation used for expenditures for electioneering communications shall be reportable and all contributions made by such membership organization or corporation which are otherwise reportable under the provisions of this Chapter shall be reported. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))
  • All other expenditures made by a membership organization or business entity which are otherwise reportable under the provisions of this Chapter shall be reported. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii))

Prohibitions

  • No person shall make or cause to be made any electioneering communication that portrays a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that is, through the use of artificial intelligence, created, altered, or digitally manipulated in a manner that would falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall and that would falsely appear to replace an individual's likeness with the likeness of a candidate or an elected official subject to recall without providing a clear and understandable disclosure on the electioneering communication that it was created using artificial intelligence. (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))

Penalties and enforcement

Whoever violates any provision of this Section with the intent to injure the reputation of a candidate or elected official subject to recall or to otherwise deceive a voter shall be fined not more than two thousand dollars or be imprisoned, with or without hard labor, for not more than two years, or both. (R.S. 18:1463(H)) The text does not state which agency enforces this provision or whether there is a private right of action.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organization deploying artificial intelligence to create, alter, or digitally manipulate an electioneering communication that portrays a candidate or elected official subject to recall must include a clear and understandable disclosure that the communication was created using artificial intelligence, in a form consistent with the disclosure requirements of R.S. 18:1463(E). (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))
  • An organization that makes expenditures for electioneering communications, including digital material placed or promoted on public facing websites or applications, must file reports if those expenditures exceed one thousand dollars in the aggregate during the aggregating period. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1), R.S. 18:1463(G)(1))
  • Coordinated expenditures for electioneering communications are treated as contributions to the candidate or committee that cooperated, consulted, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator, which may trigger contribution limits and reporting. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii), R.S. 18:1483(8))
  • A media entity that broadcasts a paid political announcement, advertisement, or electioneering communication in which the broadcaster has had no input in or control over the announcement, advertisement, or electioneering communication is exempt from the provisions of this Section. (R.S. 18:1463(I))
  • Communications by a membership organization or business entity to its employees, members, directors, or stockholders, or their family members, are excluded from the definition of expenditure if the organization is not organized primarily for political purposes, but other expenditures for electioneering communications remain reportable. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii))

Notable exemptions

  • The provisions of this Section shall not apply to a media entity that broadcasts a paid political announcement, advertisement, or electioneering communication in which the broadcaster has had no input in or control over the announcement, advertisement, or electioneering communication. (R.S. 18:1463(I))
  • Expenditure shall not include any communication, including an electioneering communication, by any membership organization or business entity to its employees, members, directors, or stockholders, or their family members, if such membership organization or business entity is not organized primarily for the purpose of supporting, opposing, or otherwise influencing the nomination for election, or election, of any person to public office or for the purpose of supporting or opposing a proposition or question to be submitted to the voters making electioneering communications. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii))
  • Contribution shall not include any dues or membership fees of any membership organization or corporation made by its members or stockholders, if such membership organization or corporation is not organized primarily for the purpose of supporting, opposing or otherwise influencing the nomination for election, or election, of any person to public office making expenditures for electioneering communications. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether a communication qualifies as an electioneering communication under R.S. 18:1483(33)(a).
  • If artificial intelligence is used to create, alter, or digitally manipulate the image, likeness, or voice of a candidate or elected official subject to recall in an electioneering communication, include a clear and understandable disclosure that it was created using artificial intelligence, consistent with R.S. 18:1463(E). (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))
  • Ensure the communication does not falsely appear to a reasonable observer to be an authentic record of actual speech or conduct or falsely appear to replace an individual's likeness with the likeness of a candidate or elected official subject to recall without the disclosure. (R.S. 18:1463(F)(1))
  • Track all expenditures for electioneering communications, including digital material placed or promoted for a fee. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1), R.S. 18:1463(G)(1))
  • If expenditures for electioneering communications exceed one thousand dollars in the aggregate during the aggregating period, file reports as required. (R.S. 18:1501.1(A)(1))
  • Treat coordinated expenditures for electioneering communications as contributions to the candidate or committee that cooperated, consulted, or acted in concert with the creator or disseminator. (R.S. 18:1483(7)(b)(ii), R.S. 18:1483(8))
  • If operating as a media entity, ensure no input in or control over paid political announcements, advertisements, or electioneering communications to qualify for the exemption. (R.S. 18:1463(I))
  • If a membership organization or business entity, report all other expenditures for electioneering communications that are otherwise reportable, even if internal communications to employees, members, directors, or stockholders are excluded. (R.S. 18:1483(11)(d)(ii), R.S. 18:1483(7)(c)(ii))
